title: SDK Sandbox Lab — daily digest and action map
content:
Context:
This doc captures the daily standup/digest from the SDK Sandbox Lab session on 2026-05-19. Purpose: keep a short public log of triage, decisions and owners for the quickstarts/samples backlog during the weeklong sandbox sprint. This is intentionally lightweight — notes + concrete next steps so other teams can pick up work if needed.

Attendees:
- Marcus Lee (owner)
- Ava Kumar (samples)
- Priya Patel (docs)
- Diego Alvarez (telemetry)
- Samira Hassan (onboarding + QA)
- Optional: a couple of people dropped in from platform and solutions for short syncs

Top-of-mind for today:
1) Quickstart reproducibility: intermittent failures on mac M2 when running local spinup.sh; appears to be a path/env issue with pyenv and brew python. Failing tests: sample-e2e/hello-world start-up healthcheck (timeout at 35s).
2) SDK 0.9.3 beta: release candidate blocked by failing example for function-calling example (PR 842). The failure surfaced due to a mismatch in streaming protocol expectations between the example and the new SDK helper.
3) Telemetry gaps: quickstart telemetry is only recording 'start' and 'end' events; missing per-step timing for install, model pull, and first inference.
4) Docs ergonomics: Quickstart landing page assumes user has a Redwood API key pre-configured; need a gating paragraph and troubleshooting section.

Decisions made:
- Prioritize reproducibility fixes in the following order: local mac M2 environment fixes (critical), CI flakiness triage (next), SDK example fixes (parallel).
- Roll forward SDK 0.9.3 GA only after PRs #842 and #854 are green and the hello-world e2e passes on mac CI.
- Add a short troubleshooting subsection to the quickstart readme rather than overhauling the whole landing page for this sprint.

Blockers / unresolved questions:
- mac M2 failures are not yet reproduced on our linux runners; do we add a macOS runner to CI? (cost implications).
- Do we standardize on pyproject + poetry inside samples or leave a thin wrapper using pip for simplicity? Engineering prefers one toolchain but samples maintainers want lower cognitive load.
- Who will own telemetry schema changes? Product wants per-step timing across quickstarts but that requires a small schema bump.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Ava: add explicit pyenv/python3.11 fallback and update spinup.sh for mac quirks; PR to samples repo by 2026-05-21. (blocking)
- Diego: add instrumentation events for install, model-pull, first-inference; draft telemetry schema change and post on #devexp-telemetry by 2026-05-20.
- Priya: add troubleshooting subsection to quickstart landing README and a one-paragraph API-key prep note; push docs commit by 2026-05-20.
- Marcus: coordinate with infra about adding one macOS self-hosted runner for nightly CI; raise cost/benefit in infra-ops sync by 2026-05-22.
- Samira: create a short checklist for QA to reproduce the failure locally and capture logs; attach to LINEAR-4472 by 2026-05-20.
- All: re-run e2e matrix after fixes; target green on mac matrix by 2026-05-24.

Notes from triage:
- PR #842: function-calling example failure looks like a small behavior change in streaming chunk boundaries introduced in SDK helper. Short-term fix: adjust example to use chunk-accumulation helper. Longer-term: add a streaming helper wrapper to the SDK that maintains backward compatibility.
- PR #854: flaky mock server teardown is causing occasional port conflicts in CI; workaround added in the PR but needs proper fix in test harness.
- Sample 'hello corpus' dataset: large sample artifacts cause long docker image builds for local testing — recommend switching to a tiny synthetic dataset for local dev and keeping full dataset for CI only.

Quick wins / small experiments to unblock users:
- Publish a tiny 'dev-mode' tag for the local quickstart docker image to speed iteration. (Ava to prototype).
- Add a small preflight shell script that verifies pyenv, python version, docker, and network access before starting the quickstart. If a check fails, show curated remediation steps instead of raw errors. (Samira + Priya).

Follow-ups for next standup (2026-05-20):
- Status on PRs #842, #854, and samples spinup fix.
- Diego to show telemetry patch and example events that will be emitted for a single quickstart run.
- Infra to report on feasibility/cost for mac runner.

Context links and references:
- GH PR for SDK example fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/842
- LINEAR ticket for reproducibility: LINEAR-4472
- Confluence sandbox ops: confluence:redwood/devexp/sandbox-ops
- Slack channels: #devexp, #devexp-telemetry, #platform-ci

Notes-to-self / informal bits:
- Keep the daily digest terse; this is the thing folks should skim for owners and deadlines.
- If infra says mac runner is too expensive, we pivot to a reproducible mac troubleshooting doc + recorded screencast from a maintainer.
- Consider a short 'how to reproduce locally' template that every sample author fills when opening a samples PR — will save hours in triage.

Closing: next check-in 2026-05-20 10:00 PT. If anything becomes urgent ping @devexp on slack.
